result:
The proposed answer, j = 1 − n, is wrong because it rests on a false claim about negative K-theory.

The solution says the Antieau–Gepner–Heller examples have a bounded t-structure with K₋₁(𝒞) ≠ 0. This reverses their result. Antieau–Gepner–Heller (building on Neeman) show that a small stable ∞-category with a bounded t-structure always has K₋₁(𝒞) = 0. So the comparison map K_j(𝒞^♡) → K_j(𝒞) is already an isomorphism for all j ≥ −1, with no Ext hypothesis at all. The guaranteed range at n = 1 therefore reaches at least j = −1, while the proposed formula gives only j ≥ 0.

The solution's bookkeeping is also off. The first possible defect in Ext^{n+1} does not first show up in K₋ₙ. The correct shift is one step further down, so the isomorphism range is j ≥ −n−1 (from my recollection of the Ext-condition theorem, not re-derived here). This matches the n = 0 case, where only Hom is an isomorphism and AGH gives j ≥ −1.

The expected answer is therefore j = −n−1 (or at the very least something below 1 − n), not 1 − n.

VERDICT: REJECT
